investigation: Isoscalar (T=0) vs Isovector (T=1) Pairing Competition and Cross-Mass Quenching
description: Systematic evaluation of neutron-proton pairing across self-conjugate (N=Z) to asymmetric (N>Z) nuclei in A~48 (Cr), A~64 (Ge), and A~92-96 (Pd), establishing the Sarma-Clogston Fermi mismatch collapse of T=0 pairing.

systems.structure_description: Self-Conjugate Collective Rotor / Max T=0/T=1 Competition
N>Z Nucleus: T=0 Quenched by Fermi Asymmetry
Spin-Aligned np Phase (J=9+ g9/2 coupling) / Equidistant Spectrum
N>Z Nucleus: Seniority-Type Spectrum / T=0 Collapse
N=50 Closed Shell: Pure Proton Hole Seniority Spectrum

boundary_1_fermi_mismatch_pair_breaking.mechanism: In self-conjugate nuclei (92Pd), identical neutron and proton Fermi surfaces (lambda_n = lambda_p) enable robust isoscalar T=0 spin-aligned Cooper pairs (J=9+ g9/2 coupling), producing a regular, nearly equidistant vibrational-like spectrum. Adding just 2 neutrons separates the Fermi surfaces by delta_lambda = 2*C_sym*|N-Z|/A = 1.22 MeV. Because delta_lambda exceeds the Sarma-Clogston critical limit Delta_0/sqrt(2) = 0.88 MeV, the T=0 pairing condensate abruptly collapses via first-order phase transition to Delta_T0 = 0, causing E(2+) to jump from 874 keV to 1412 keV and restoring pure isovector like-particle seniority structure.
boundary_1_fermi_mismatch_pair_breaking.failure_signature: Disappearance of T=0 pairing gaps and sharp change in excitation spectrum upon stepping from N=Z to |N-Z| >= 2.

boundary_2_spin_aligned_vs_collective_co.contrast: J=9+ aligned pair coupling vs macroscopic BCS condensate
boundary_2_spin_aligned_vs_collective_co.mechanism: The low-lying spectrum of 92Pd does not exhibit true macroscopic BCS collective condensation (which requires infinite-range pairing across multiple j-shells), but rather finite-valence valence-space recoupling of spin-aligned (g9/2)^2_J=9+ proton-neutron pairs with constant energy steps Delta E ~ 500 keV.
boundary_2_spin_aligned_vs_collective_co.failure_signature: Lack of rotational I(I+1) collectivity despite strong np correlations.
